patient.name: Walter Higgins
patient.chiefComplaint: Weakness and shortness of breath, three days after a heart attack

history.hpi: Discharged home yesterday after a STEMI treated with emergent PCI and stent placement three days ago. Wife found him this afternoon pale, weak, and short of breath sitting on the edge of the bed, unable to walk to the bathroom without nearly collapsing. He denies chest pain currently but reports feeling 'wiped out' and lightheaded when he tries to stand.
history.lastOralIntake: Sips of water this morning; no solid food since last night
history.events: Wife called 911 after finding him pale, diaphoretic, and short of breath in the bedroom; he nearly collapsed attempting to walk to the bathroom

scene.dispatch: 68-year-old male, difficulty breathing and weakness, residence
scene.location: Single-story home, bedroom, patient sitting on the edge of the bed leaning forward
scene.bystanders: Wife present; reports he was hospitalized for a heart attack and discharged home yesterday
visualCues: Hospital discharge paperwork and pill bottles on the nightstand
Labored breathing with mild accessory muscle use
Cool, mottled skin on hands and feet

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew finds a 68-year-old male three days post-MI, pale and diaphoretic, sitting on the edge of the bed leaning forward. He is weak, mildly dyspneic, with cool mottled skin and weak peripheral pulses, consistent with early cardiogenic shock.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Mildly labored, bibasilar crackles on auscultation, RR 26
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Weak, thready radial pulses; cool, mottled skin on hands and feet
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Strength intact in all extremities, though generally weak and fatigued
otherFindings: Bibasilar crackles, worse at the bases
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I just feel so weak... I got dizzy trying to walk to the bathroom."

transitions.if: IV access, ASA, and cautious fluid bolus given
transitions.condition: Crew establishes IV access, applies cardiac monitor/defib pads, acquires a 12-lead EKG, administers aspirin, and gives a cautious 250-500 mL fluid bolus given the SBP <100 mmHg.

phases.name: IV access, ASA, and cautious fluid bolus given
phases.description: Crew places IV access, applies the cardiac monitor and defib pads, obtains a 12-lead EKG, gives aspirin, and administers a cautious 250-500 mL fluid bolus given the hypotension, while watching closely for signs of fluid overload before considering any repeat bolus.
phases.triggerCondition: After recognizing hypotension and poor perfusion in a recent post-MI patient, the crew establishes IV access, places monitor/defib pads, obtains a 12-lead EKG, gives aspirin, and administers one cautious fluid bolus per the SBP <100 mmHg guidance, planning to reassess for rales or hepatomegaly before any repeat.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Weak radial pulses, cool mottled skin, IV established in the left AC
otherFindings: 12-lead EKG shows sinus tachycardia, no acute ST elevation
250 mL NS bolus infused, reassessing lung sounds before considering repeat
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "That water in my lungs feeling... it's still there a little."

expectedActions.shortAction: Establish IV access; if unable within 2 attempts/90 seconds, place an IO
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Establish IV access. If unable to obtain within two attempts or less than 90 seconds, place an IO needle
expectedActions.rationale: Vascular access is required for fluids and vasopressor support in shock.

expectedActions.shortAction: Acquire 12-lead EKG within 10 minutes; transmit for STEMI interpretation
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: It is imperative that EMS clinicians routinely acquire a 12-lead EKG within 10 minutes for all patients exhibiting signs and symptoms of ACS
expectedActions.rationale: Rules out a new active STEMI as the cause of decompensation in this recent post-MI patient.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Chest Pain/Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)/ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)

expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Administer aspirin; chewable, non-enteric-coated aspirin preferred (162–325 mg)
expectedActions.rationale: Standard ACS therapy given recent MI, even without current chest pain.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Chest Pain/Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)/ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)

expectedActions.shortAction: Give a cautious 250-500 mL IV fluid bolus given SBP <100 mmHg
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: SBP less than 100 mmHg i. IV fluid bolus 250–500 mL
expectedActions.rationale: A small, cautious bolus is appropriate first-line for hypotension, but must be limited given cardiogenic shock risk.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Respiratory Distress (includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema)

expectedActions.shortAction: Place defibrillator pads and maintain continuous cardiac monitoring
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Consider placing defibrillator pads on high-risk patients
expectedActions.rationale: Recent MI with hemodynamic instability carries elevated dysrhythmia risk.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Chest Pain/Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)/ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess breath sounds and JVD before considering any repeat fluid bolus
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: If the patient condition deteriorates after fluid administration, rales or hepatomegaly develop, then consider cardiogenic shock and withholding further fluid administration
expectedActions.rationale: Repeating fluid boluses without reassessment risks worsening cardiogenic pulmonary edema.

transitions.condition: Blood pressure remains low despite the cautious fluid bolus; the crew withholds further fluid and initiates a norepinephrine infusion per the fluid-refractory hypotension guidance.
Crew repeats the fluid bolus without reassessing breath sounds or JVD, worsening the underlying cardiogenic pulmonary edema.

phases.name: Fluid-refractory, norepinephrine started
phases.description: Blood pressure remains low despite the cautious fluid bolus and crackles are unchanged. The crew withholds further fluid, initiates a norepinephrine infusion titrated to blood pressure, and provides advance notification to the receiving hospital.
phases.triggerCondition: Reassessment after the initial fluid bolus shows persistent hypotension without worsening rales, so the crew withholds further fluid and starts a titrated norepinephrine infusion, consistent with vasopressor guidance for fluid-refractory shock.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Norepinephrine infusion running via the established IV; radial pulses slightly stronger
otherFindings: Norepinephrine infusion titrating upward toward goal MAP
Advance notification given to receiving hospital
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I think I feel a little steadier now."

expectedActions.shortAction: Start norepinephrine infusion at 1.8 mcg/min (90 kg × 0.02 mcg/kg/min); titrate to SBP >90 mmHg
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: SBP less than 100 mmHg ii. Consider vasopressor: Norepinephrine 0.02–2 mcg/kg/min
expectedActions.rationale: Fluid-refractory hypotension in cardiogenic shock requires titrated vasopressor support rather than further fluid.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Respiratory Distress (includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema)

expectedActions.shortAction: Provide advance notification to the receiving hospital
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Provide advance notification to the hospital
expectedActions.rationale: Cardiogenic shock post-MI requires hospital preparation for possible cath lab or ICU-level care.

transitions.condition: Blood pressure trends upward on the norepinephrine infusion, mentation remains intact, and the crew proceeds with transport with serial reassessment.

phases.name: Perfusion improves, transport initiated
phases.description: Blood pressure has improved on the titrated norepinephrine infusion. The patient is transported with serial vital sign and neurologic reassessment to a facility capable of managing post-MI cardiogenic shock.
phases.triggerCondition: After the norepinephrine infusion is titrated and blood pressure trends upward with stable mentation, the crew proceeds with transport, reassessing frequently for signs of recurrent decompensation.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses stronger, skin warming slightly
otherFindings: Norepinephrine infusion titrated to maintain SBP >90 mmHg
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Thank you, I feel a bit more myself."

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess vital signs and neurologic status serially en route, at least every 15 minutes
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Full vital signs (pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate, neurologic status assessment) with reassessment q 15 minutes or more frequently as appropriate
expectedActions.rationale: Cardiogenic shock patients can decompensate quickly; frequent reassessment catches deterioration early.

phases.name: Fluid bolus repeated without reassessment
phases.description: The crew repeats the fluid bolus without reassessing breath sounds or JVD. The underlying cardiogenic pulmonary edema worsens, with increasing crackles, hypoxia, and respiratory distress.
phases.triggerCondition: The crew repeats the fluid bolus without reassessing for rales or hepatomegaly, precipitating worsening cardiogenic pulmonary edema.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Worsening crackles throughout both lung fields, RR 32, accessory muscle use
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Weak thready pulses, skin remains cool and mottled
otherFindings: Crackles now audible throughout both lung fields

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize iatrogenic pulmonary edema; stop fluids, support ventilation, start norepinephrine
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: If the patient condition deteriorates after fluid administration, rales or hepatomegaly develop, then consider cardiogenic shock and withholding further fluid administration
expectedActions.rationale: Recognizing and correcting fluid-overload from a repeated bolus is necessary to prevent further respiratory failure.
